public_rationale: On the ordinary capability reading, substantial improvement had occurred before the post. METR measured sustained gains in task-completion ability, and Stanford documented large benchmark gains. Persistent unreliability is real, but it does not establish stagnation. A narrower claim that models had not become dependable replacements for workers would require a different assessment.
limitations: The result depends on interpreting 'meaningful improvement' as substantial capability gains.
Benchmark progress does not establish proportional improvements in workplace productivity.
Some comparisons measure complete systems, including tools and prompting.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI models have not shown meaningful improvement over the past few years.

statement.excerpt: The expectation that generative AI will transform into something much, much more powerful requires you to first ignore the existing limitations, believing it to be more capable than it is, and also ignore the fact that these models have yet to show meaningful improvement over the past few years.

from_speaker: have yet to show meaningful improvement
our_interpretation: I read 'the past few years' as approximately 2022 through the post date, April 28, 2025.

The plain reading is that generative models made no substantial capability gains. Meaningful improvement includes substantial gains on comparable reasoning, coding, and task-completion evaluations; it does not require eliminating hallucinations or replacing whole jobs.
I assess the historical assertion, not the surrounding argument about expectations for future AI.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations across the period show broad stagnation, with apparent gains small, unreliable, or explained by changes in testing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible longitudinal evaluations show substantial gains in important capabilities, including tasks with practical relevance.

evidence.explanation: The original evaluation finds substantial growth in the duration of software and reasoning tasks agents can complete with 50% success. Its historical comparisons include the years preceding the post, although this is a restricted task distribution.

evidence.publisher: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
evidence.explanation: The report records substantial improvement on software issue resolution and also reports gains on multimodal understanding and science questions. These are system-level benchmark comparisons, so they do not isolate changes in model weights from changes in surrounding tools.

The same researchers emphasize that substantial measured progress coexists with poor reliability on ordinary autonomous work. This supports the surrounding concern about limitations, but does not establish an absence of improvement.
